newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish BG Bank closes activists' account.
newsitem.headline: Danish BG Bank closes activists' account.

text.p: Denmark's BG Bank said on Wednesday it had cancelled an anti-immigration organisation's account and would look at the backgrounds of other organisations which were clients.

"This is not a campaign we have suddenly launched. We have done this before. We do not want to have our name on the same giro cards as certain associations," BG spokesman Rene La Cour Sell told Reuters.

"You could say we are practising ethical banking but European Union directives encourage banks to exercise vigilance over clients," Sell said. "It is not just racist bodies or fascist groups we want to blacklist, it could also be activists of any sort."
BG Bank, Denmark's third-biggest bank, was formed in January 1996 from the merger of the former Bikuben savings bank and the post office Giro Bank.

Sell said that virtually all Danish societies, associations and clubs had accounts with the old Giro Bank before the merger, hence the need to look into organisational clients' political and moral background.
"BG Bank is not conducting a witch hunt against potentially subversive groups in Danish society. It is important to say that we are not just indulging in political correctness," Sell said.
